question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases (PED) under the Optima Care health policy?
expected_answer: Pre-existing diseases are subject to a mandatory waiting period of 36 months of continuous coverage before claims are payable.

question: How many days of pre-hospitalization and post-hospitalization expenses are covered?
expected_answer: Pre-hospitalization expenses are covered up to 60 days prior to admission, and post-hospitalization expenses are covered up to 180 days following discharge.

question: Is cataract surgery subject to any monetary sub-limit?
expected_answer: Yes, cataract surgery is capped at a maximum of ₹40,000 per eye under Plan A, and ₹60,000 per eye under Plan B.

question: Under what circumstance is dental surgery or treatment covered in health insurance?
expected_answer: Dental treatment or surgery is excluded unless it requires in-patient hospitalization necessitated by an accidental bodily injury.

question: What is the compulsory deductible for a private car with engine capacity exceeding 1,500 cc?
expected_answer: The compulsory deductible is ₹2,000 per claim for private cars with engine capacity exceeding 1,500 cc (and ₹1,000 for engines not exceeding 1,500 cc).

question: What threshold qualifies a damaged car as a Constructive Total Loss (CTL)?
expected_answer: A vehicle is considered a Constructive Total Loss when the aggregate cost of retrieval and repair exceeds 75% of the Insured Declared Value (IDV).

question: What depreciation percentage is deducted on rubber parts and airbags in partial loss motor claims?
expected_answer: A 50% depreciation rate is deducted on rubber, nylon, plastic parts, tyres, tubes, batteries, and airbags.

question: Does the base car insurance cover engine damage caused by water ingression or hydrostatic lock?
expected_answer: No, damage caused by water ingression or hydrostatic lock from attempting to restart an inundated vehicle is excluded under base cover unless an Engine Protector add-on is active.

question: How many consecutive claim-free years are needed to reach the maximum 50% No Claim Bonus (NCB)?
expected_answer: 5 consecutive claim-free years are required to reach the maximum NCB discount of 50%.

question: Within how many days can a policyholder cancel their health policy under the Free-Look period?
expected_answer: A policyholder has 15 days from physical receipt of the policy document (or 30 days for electronic/distance marketing policies) to cancel during the Free-Look Period.

question: What is the maximum dispute claim value that can be submitted to the Insurance Ombudsman?
expected_answer: The total claim value, including compensation sought, must not exceed ₹30,00,000 (Rupees Thirty Lakhs) to fall under Ombudsman jurisdiction.

question: What penalty interest must an insurer pay if claim payment is delayed beyond 30 days?
expected_answer: The insurer must pay penal interest at 2% above the prevailing RBI Bank Rate from the date of final document receipt until the date of payment.
